meta.title: Pricing — Syncologic
meta.description: Plans for how you transfer — Free, Pro, Business, and Private Runner. Join the waitlist for early access.

hero.headline: Pick the plan that matches how you transfer.
hero.subheading: Four plans, four ways our users transfer. Pick yours and join the waitlist for early access.

hypotheses.title: Four plans
hypotheses.subtitle: Each plan maps to a clear use case. Pick the one that fits you.

free.name: Free
features: Browser Runner only — tab stays open
One source + destination at a time
Up to a few GB per transfer
free.footnote: For one-off transfers and trying Syncologic before paying.

pro.name: Pro
pro.footnote: For individuals who want hosted, scheduled transfers without keeping a tab open.

business.name: Business
features: Higher data volumes and parallel jobs
business.footnote: For teams migrating a workspace or running multiple jobs in parallel.

privateRunner.name: Private Runner
features: Run transfers on your own server, NAS, or VPS
Pay for the control plane, not for bandwidth
privateRunner.footnote: For users who bring their own infrastructure. Bytes and credentials stay with you.

affects.title: What affects cost
affects.subtitle: Three factors shape what your plan should look like.

volume.title: Data volume
volume.body: The biggest single driver — how much data moves per job and per month.

frequency.title: Frequency
frequency.body: One-time migrations, recurring backups, and continuous sync each price differently.

runner.title: Runner choice
runner.body: Cloud Runner uses our bandwidth. Browser and Private Runner don't.

cloudVsPrivate.title: Cloud Runner vs Private Runner economics
cloudVsPrivate.subtitle: Same control plane, different data path. Pick what fits your trust and volume.

rows.private: Control plane only — flat per-month fee.

rows.cloud: Convenience, scheduled jobs, migrations you don't want to babysit.
rows.private: Privacy, homelabs, businesses, high-volume users on their own bandwidth.

earlyAccess.headline: Join now, lock in early access.
earlyAccess.body: Nobody pays yet. Waitlist members get the first invitations at launch.

items.a: The four-plan structure is set. Exact prices may shift at the margins before launch — that's why each tier shows a `~` instead of an exact number.

items.q: Will the Private Runner cost more than the Cloud Runner?
items.a: Less. You bring the bandwidth, so Private Runner is a flat control-plane fee instead of metered usage.
We plan a path toward source-visible, self-hostable infrastructure. Pricing for that path will be set when the model itself is set — see the self-hosted page for details.

items.q: Will I be charged automatically when launch happens?
items.a: No. Joining the waitlist never bills you. Anyone moving from waitlist to a paid plan does so explicitly.

items.q: What happens if my use case spans two plans?
items.a: Pick the closer one and tell us in the waitlist questions. We'll reach out before launch if a different plan fits better.

preview.title: See what will happen first
preview.desc: Before anything moves, we show you which files will be copied, replaced, or left alone — so there are no surprises.

scoped.title: We only ask for what we need
scoped.desc: When you connect Google Drive or another cloud, we ask for the smallest permission to do the job — nothing more.

progress.title: Watch it work in real time
progress.desc: See how many files have moved, how much is left, and roughly how long until it's done.

reports.title: A clear summary at the end
reports.desc: Every transfer ends with a simple report you can save or share, so you know exactly what happened.

transparency.title: You choose where your files go
transparency.desc: Run the transfer through us, in your browser, or on your own computer. Your call, every time.

developers.title: Developers — automate cloud file transfers
developers.description: Move files between clouds with a typed HTTP API, a CLI, webhooks, and runners you can host yourself.
developers.heroHeadline: Move files between clouds with one API.
developers.heroSubheading: For agencies, SaaS teams, and internal tools that move files between cloud providers without writing the glue.
developers.audienceLabel: Built for agencies, SaaS engineering teams, platform groups, and internal tooling.
developers.apiBody: Create a job with a source, destination, runner, and optional schedule. The control plane validates, dispatches, and emits progress events.
developers.apiCaption: Sketch — final shape will land with the v1 API.
developers.cliTitle: A CLI for scripts and CI
developers.cliBody: Same jobs, driven from a terminal or a CI runner. Useful for one-shot migrations and for backups owned by a script you can read in a code review.
developers.cliCaption: Planned. Behavior mirrors the API one-to-one.
developers.runnersTitle: Pick the runner that fits the job
developers.runnersBody: Same API. Three different data paths. Choose per job, not per account.

runnerCloud.title: Cloud Runner
runnerCloud.desc: Hosted runners for scheduled jobs and large migrations. No infrastructure on your side.

runnerBrowser.title: Browser Runner
runnerBrowser.desc: For ad-hoc transfers from a tab. The data path stays in the user's browser; no long-lived tokens.

runnerPrivate.title: Private Runner
runnerPrivate.desc: Self-host the runner binary in your VPC, on-prem, or on a NAS. Outbound-only connection to the control plane.

developers.webhooksTitle: Webhooks for the events you care about
developers.webhooksBody: Subscribe to job lifecycle events and stream them into your queue, your dashboard, or your audit log. Payloads will be HMAC-signed.
developers.noSdkBody: We will not ship an official SDK before the API is stable. The OpenAPI spec will be public, so you can generate a typed client in any language you already use.

faq.a: We're not committing to a date. The API ships with the first paid Cloud Runner tier — join the waitlist for early access.

faq.q: Will there be a free tier for developers?
faq.a: There's no special developer offer — everything you'd pay (or not pay) is in the current plans.

faq.q: Do you handle OAuth on behalf of my users?
faq.a: Yes. Users connect their cloud accounts to Syncologic — not to your app. You don't store provider credentials; the control plane manages the OAuth lifecycle.

faq.q: Can I run jobs entirely on my own infrastructure?
faq.a: Yes for the data path — Private Runner runs in your VPC, NAS, or any machine you control, and file bytes never reach Syncologic. The control plane (accounts, jobs, schedules) is hosted by us at launch; full self-host is on the roadmap.
Webhook payloads will be HMAC-signed with a per-workspace secret you control.

meta.title: Self-hosted future — Syncologic
meta.description: Source-visible, self-hostable cloud file transfer. Private Runner first, then full self-host, then air-gapped — on your timeline.

hero.headline: Source-visible. Self-hostable. Yours to run.
hero.subheading: Source-visible runner at launch. Self-hostable control plane on the roadmap.
hero.audience: For homelab operators, privacy-conscious users, and businesses that want their file transfers running on infrastructure they control.

principles.title: Architecture principles
principles.intro: We separate the metadata layer from where files actually move. That split is what makes self-hosting tractable.

controlPlane.title: Control plane
controlPlane.desc: Accounts, jobs, schedules, reports. The metadata layer — hosted by us at launch, self-hostable on the roadmap.

dataPlane.title: Data plane
dataPlane.desc: Where bytes flow. Source → runner → destination. Self-host the runner from launch; bytes never reach the control plane.

principles.note: Files do not flow through our server. The server holds metadata; the runner moves the bytes.

privateRunner.title: Private Runner: available first
privateRunner.body: Run transfers on your own machine, NAS, or VPS at launch. Your provider credentials and file bytes stay with you; the control plane only holds job metadata.

outbound.title: Outbound only
outbound.desc: Your runner reaches out to us. No inbound ports, no exposed services.

credentials.title: Credentials stay with you
credentials.desc: Provider tokens live where your runner runs. We never see them.

dataPath.title: Direct data path
dataPath.desc: Files flow source → your runner → destination. Nothing in between.

futureModel.title: Future self-host levels
futureModel.label: On the roadmap
futureModel.intro: Three levels of self-hosting, in increasing independence from our infrastructure.

level1.name: Private Runner
level1.desc: Hosted control plane, your data path. For users who want our convenience and your bandwidth.

level2.name: Full self-host
level2.desc: Bring your own control plane. Your auth, your database, your runners. Same product, your infrastructure.

level3.name: Air-gapped
level3.desc: No outbound dependency on syncologic.com. For high-compliance environments that can't reach the public internet.

sourceTrust.title: Why core code stays public
sourceTrust.body: Runner code, transfer logic, and provider adapters will ship source-visible. You'll be able to audit how files move before trusting the system.
